sentences: A constant-space resolution refutation keeps only a bounded amount of the specified proof information at any moment.
The saved question asks whether such formulas always have refutations that are also polynomial in length.
The same derivation must satisfy both requirements, which is stronger than obtaining each bound separately.
A positive result would rule out an unavoidable recomputation penalty for the most memory-frugal proofs.
The source summary does not reproduce its space-measure convention, so that definition and the allowed constant dependence still need to accompany a complete formulation.
